paragraphs: Propel makes a mobile app for people who receive government benefits on an EBT card, pitched on its own site as the simplest way to check a balance and save money. The app itself costs nothing to use.

With the cardholder's permission, Propel connects to their state benefits portal. It then gathers the EBT balance and transaction history, makes that easier to read, and displays it in the app. That spares people from calling a 1-800 number or logging in to a state website. Balance checking works in 49 states, the District of Columbia, and several U.S. territories. Iowa is the exception. The app also carries card security features such as suspicious activity monitoring and out of state transaction blocking.

The company says it was founded to make government benefits better at the speed and scale recipients deserve. The company points to more than a million 5-star reviews of the app. Money comes from advertising. Most of the promotions are free or discounted services available only to EBT cardholders. Propel also runs surveys that reach millions of users nationwide. It says those findings give insight to policymakers working to improve state and federal benefits programs.

quote.text: We founded Propel to build technology that makes people’s government benefits better, at the speed and scale they deserve.
